quest.title: The Four at Loggerheads
quest.description: You have temporarily lost Nahida's help, but according to the message she left behind, you will meet someone in the desert who can help you get out of the woods. To foil the nefarious plot between the Akademiya and the Fatui, you set off on another journey.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x775, Primogem x30, Mora x31175, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've finally made it to Caravan Ribat. It's pretty lively here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So just past this wall is the desert, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh wow, Paimon remembers hearing people call this the Wall of Samiel. It's made to block sandstorms from the outside... If it's this tall, it's gotta be the divine work of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, right?

choices.text: It is indeed quite impressive...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: ...Enough gawking. Come on, follow me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh...?

choices.text: Alhaitham!?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Over here.

choices.text: (Where did he come from...?)
Truly awe-inspiring.

dialogues.speaker: Eremite Mercenary
dialogues.text: #What the? Where did {M#he}{F#she} go!?

dialogues.speaker: Eremite Mercenary
dialogues.text: Ugh, how did we lose 'em? They were just here a second ago...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: More Eremite mercenaries? Who're they working for this time... Anyway, Traveler, it seems like we were being followed again!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You were too careless. You should have noticed those hopeless amateurs trailing you a long time ago.

choices.text: Thanks, Alhaitham.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: There's no need to thank me. I've never cared to keep track of personal favors.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: All I did was correct a mistake I happened to come across. It's a habit I developed at the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You really gave Paimon a scare, Alhaitham! We never thought we'd run into you here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Last time we met at Port Ormos, didn't you say you were going back to the Akademiya? Wait... don't tell Paimon that you're here to take us back on their orders!

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Oh, so you've already landed yourselves on the Akademiya's hit list? Haha, I can't say that I didn't expect it.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: However, had I wished to turn you over to the Akademiya, don't you think you'd already be the Eremites' honored guests by now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right... You do have a point.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Did you participate in the sages' big project?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I have no interest in running errands for that project. As a scholar, I've always belonged to the camp that promotes researcher autonomy.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: And these days, you are more fascinating than anything the sages can offer.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, you were actually looking for me?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Hmm, not quite. To tell you the truth... I'm still investigating the Divine Knowledge Capsule. Unfortunately, I've run into some difficulties.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Everyone says the capsule originated in the desert and was eventually moved to Port Ormos. If I am to get to the bottom of this, I must understand how the capsule first came to be.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Which brings me back to you, and why you're so interesting.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: The leader of Ayn Al-Ahmar used the Divine Knowledge Capsule right in front of you, and upon seeing him, your expression became perplexed, and you were lost in thought for quite some time.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: To have that kind of reaction, I think you must have realized something. Are you interested at all in sharing what you've been hiding from me?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (It must be because I was so shocked to hear those words again... "world... forget me...")

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alhaitham, you really have a ridiculous eye for detail! What kind of person even notices and remembers stuff like that...

choices.text: The situation is a little complicated.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: So that's your answer... Well, I do work for the Akademiya after all. So considering that, it is indeed wise to keep your cards close to your chest.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: But that does prove you do have some undisclosed information about the Divine Knowledge Capsule. Am I right?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: No matter. Rather than simply learning the answers from you, I'd still prefer to investigate on my own. Speaking of, you two are also headed to the desert?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, we have the same plan as you. But we don't really have any concrete goals at the moment...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Then I'd suggest starting with Aaru Village. It's the largest settlement in the desert, so it'll probably have more resources and intel than anywhere else. Well? Would you like to head there together?

choices.text: Sounds good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's always better to travel with someone you know. Let's go!

choices.text: Let's head there together then.
I can't share what I know just yet.
We couldn't have shaken them without you.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Before us lies Aaru Village, the safe haven of the desert folk.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, this landscape is really something else. What a cool place! Let's go check it out!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Unless my memory fails me, we have barely spoken two words to each other before now at the Akademiya. Would you care to enlighten me as to when and how I invited the General Mahamatra's wrath?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Alhaitham, do not think you can escape my judgment just because you managed to escape my attack.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: "Judgment"? So, that's how you'd characterize your actions here, is it? Or would "elimination" perhaps be a more accurate description?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Had I used my full strength, not even this traveler would have been able to stop me.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Though styled like an assassination, I sought only to ensure that my target would be unable to flee or resist. Standard practice for the matra, as well you know.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Seemed to me more like your own personal touch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, wh—who is that, Alhaitham? Did you call him "General Mahamatra"?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Yes... General Mahamatra Cyno, head of all the matra at the Akademiya. He's a formidable hunter, and the ultimate nightmare for any who have committed academic crimes.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You seem to have placed a lot of trust in Alhaitham, to the point of blocking an attack for him.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If I were you, I'd never choose to side with him. I wouldn't believe a single word that comes out of his mouth.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I have been pursuing this scribe for a long time. I urge you, stand back and do not seek to defend him any longer. Otherwise... there will be consequences.

choices.text: I don't trust him as much as you seem to think.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Has Alhaitham done something wrong? Paimon doesn't think he's as bad as you've made him out to be.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I won't waste my breath explaining things. Alhaitham, I saw it during our fight...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Take it out. The Divine Knowledge Capsule you're hiding on your person. Unless you want me to retrieve it for myself?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: ...Hmph.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Very perceptive of you... Nothing escapes a matra's senses.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, the Divine Knowledge Capsule!? Didn't it fall into the matra's hands in Port Ormos?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So you did lie to us.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: No wonder you speak with such confidence, Cyno. But I must admit, I am very curious... What does this capsule mean to you?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: And why, as General Mahamatra of the Akademiya, are you all alone in the desert?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: As far as I'm aware, the other matra have been speculating about your disappearance.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Have you been given a mission that's... let's say, morally dubious?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: If I was the real target of your mission, what was stopping you from simply using your authority and resources to judge me within the walls of the Akademiya?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is it a mission from the sages?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I should have known you'd be difficult to deal with.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You two... Ugh, what should we do, {NICKNAME}? Paimon feels like we can't trust either of them...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Ahem... Well look at you two, acting all tough and self-righteous over there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, Dehya!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Great, {NICKNAME}, finally someone that we can trust!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You gotta help us out here! Otherwise, these two are gonna start fighting again...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yeah, sure looks that way... Two giants from the Akademiya, duking it out once and for all. Not something you get to see every day, that's for sure.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Listen, I know you academic types love to fill up your big brains with self-righteous morality, and lord your empty rules and virtues over each other...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: But how dare you bring your petty disputes into the safe haven of Aaru Village?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: It seems like someone's gonna have to beat some sense into your thick skulls until you finally learn to respect these grounds!

choices.text: Neither of them can afford to be distracted by Dehya...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hey! Did either of you hear a word I just said!?

response.speaker: Wind
response.text: Whoosh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! What's going on!? The wind's so strong — is this a sandstorm!? Paimon's gonna get blown away!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Tch... Another sandstorm? What's up with these recently?
Hey! All of you, over here, quickly! We have to take cover!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Someone's calling for us, {NICKNAME}! This wind is too strong. Let's get over there!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: That sounded like Candace...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...C'mon, you two! Geez, are all you Akademiya folks such hard work? Move it!

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Alright, stop yelling.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...Hmph.

choices.text: They're still looking for an opportunity to attack...
But that doesn't mean I'm going to stand by and do nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, this is pretty awkward...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Hey, wanna play sardines with three people who wanna tear each other limb from limb?" "Sure, why not, sounds fun!"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... The air's so thick and heavy, Paimon can hardly keep floating anymore...
My sincerest apologies, everyone. This is the home of our village chief. I will have to ask you to make do with this small room until the sandstorm dies down.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Please let me introduce myself. I am Candace, protector of Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, our savior has come at last!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice to meet you, Candace! The name's Paimon! Thank you so much for helping us!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You have my gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Hehe, there's no need to thank me. It's only right to help each other when the weather gets rough.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... She's so gentle and caring, like a nice older sister! ...Unlike those guys over there.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Alright, now that we're all better acquainted, we should return to the topic at hand.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: As a guardian charged with the responsibility to protect my fellow villagers from harm, I was observing your conflict from afar, even before the sandstorm started.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: And now that you have set foot within Aaru Village itself, it is all the more my responsibility to make absolutely sure that you pose no threat whatsoever to us.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: So please, have an honest and sincere conversation with one another, and put your hostile feelings to rest.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: If anyone dares to start anything again while they are under this roof... I will not hesitate to send them out for some quality time with the creatures of the sandstorm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... On second thought, Paimon may have misjudged Candace's character.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: And that goes for you too, Miss Dehya.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Do I make myself clear?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Alright, we got it, Candace.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's what I like to hear. So, which of you will begin?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I was supposed to be a mediator, but uh... I might've gotten a little too involved just now. Anyway, one of those two should probably start talking.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, that was you trying to be a mediator?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I have nothing to hide, so there is no shame in explaining myself.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: While Alhaitham wasn't wrong about the other matra not knowing my whereabouts, it's not because I've been assigned a morally dubious mission.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Rather... I've chosen to exile myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Exile yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: A little while ago, I discovered that there was data missing in the Akademiya's project planning and development files. What little they did report clearly did not match the project's actual progress.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: As General Mahamatra, I had the responsibility and authority to request an audit. However, to my surprise, the person responsible for the erroneous data was none other than Grand Sage Azar himself.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I tried to investigate the issue myself before submitting a formal audit request, but I soon found that all leads and potential pieces of incriminating evidence were carefully concealed from me.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I began to realize that... they were cautious of me from the very beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Unsurprisingly, the Grand Sage rejected my audit request as soon as the submission reached his desk. He even said to me:

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: "The power of the General Mahamatra is granted by the sages. You have no right to judge us."

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: So they really are up to no good.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I realized then that to the Grand Sage, the matra are nothing more than tools for the sages to assert and maintain their control over knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The vows that we took, the principles that we strive to uphold... They are meaningless to the Akademiya of today.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you then decided to exile yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I believed it would be wise to flee the Akademiya before the sages had a chance to take action against me. This way, they can no longer see nor predict my actions.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I will never give up on this investigation... There's no need for someone else to give me power or authority. Once I find the truth, I will administer judgment by my own name.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cyno seems to have the same goal as us... We're all investigating the sages!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Plus, now that he's no longer the General Mahamatra, he somehow feels a lot less scary!

choices.text: (It's still too early to trust him completely...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Cyno, if that's your story, then why did you see Alhaitham as a target?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: When I was investigating the matter in the Akademiya, I overheard a conversation between Alhaitham and a sage.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: #The sages asked you to investigate a {M#blond}{F#blonde}-haired Traveler. Do you dispute this, Alhaitham?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Like many parts of the project, this assignment was undocumented. Now, throw in your suspicious behavior with the Divine Knowledge Capsule, and I think we deserve an explanation.

choices.text: From the very beginning, Alhaitham was...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Yes, I was indeed tasked with investigating the Traveler.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alhaitham!

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: After all, the promised reward was so great that hardly any scholar could have refused. The sage told me, "Once you've completed this assignment, I can give you a glimpse of divine knowledge."

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: A most enticing offer.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Unfortunately, those academics don't know me at all.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Their words contained one key piece of information, namely that "Divine Knowledge" indeed exists. That gave me all I needed to know.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: From my perspective, the sages are far from trustworthy. Think about it: Isn't it a little strange that they're so willing to share Divine Knowledge with anyone, even as a reward?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: So, I began my own investigation following the lead of the Divine Knowledge Capsule. In the end, I realized my wisdom in committing to this rather than collaborating with the sages.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Had I been less guarded, I probably would have ended up like that Ayn Al-Ahmar mercenary, incapable of remaining sane for long enough to hold a conversation.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You mean that the sages originally planned to dispose of you using one of those capsules that drive people insane?

choices.text: What about your encounter with me?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I'd already given up on the assignment by then. I only told the Akademiya I was waiting in Port Ormos for you to appear so that they wouldn't suspect anything.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: So it came as quite a surprise when I encountered my erstwhile target while investigating the Divine Knowledge Capsule.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Criminals do love to talk about "coincidences."

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: #Even though I ran into {NICKNAME} by chance, I had no intention of providing assistance to the Akademiya. Also, you should remember...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: You were the ones who decided to follow me and strike up a conversation after I left that tavern.

choices.text: Now that you mention it, things did go like that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true... Alhaitham helped us out at Caravan Ribat as well. Maybe he's telling the truth?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I'm willing to apologize, if that's worth anything to you.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I took the Divine Knowledge Capsule behind your back because I judged its existence to be a significant risk. I felt that it would be best for no one to interact with it before it had been properly studied.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: After all, curiosity often proves to be the most dangerous thing in this land.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You should be well aware, Scribe Alhaitham, that curiosity can also lead you to danger and suspicion.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Answer me this: Did the sages share any information about their project with you?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Have I not made myself clear? You and I are both distrusted by the Akademiya. Do you really think they would tell me anything?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...Fine. Although you haven't completely proven your innocence, I won't regard you as an enemy for now.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: As you wish.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Mm—hmm, good. I'm glad to see you two clearing up your misunderstandings.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: And now you, Dehya. I believe it's your turn.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...Oh, sorry. Whatever the boys were talking about must have been so boring that I spaced out.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Ahem... My situation is pretty straightforward. My employer, Dunyarzad of the Homayani family, is friends with the Traveler and is currently recovering from her illness at home.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I had nothing going on, so I decided to return to Aaru Village for a visit. I was actually looking forward to a pretty exciting time getting back together with everyone here...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: But then I saw these two random guys in the middle of a pointless argument. It ticked me off, and things went downhill from there...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Is that all? Well, I will admit that definitely sounds like your style. In that case, welcome back, Dehya!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: That's more like it! I missed you all so much, Candace...
*growl*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! What was that sound?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: No need to worry. Now that you're no longer at each other's throats, please make yourselves at home. I'll take a quick trip outside to clear out some of those creatures in the sandstorm.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C—Creatures in the sandstorm...? Uh, are you sure you don't want some backup?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Fighting in a sandstorm is not for the fainthearted. Anyone without extensive training in these conditions is at a disadvantage. You needn't worry.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yeah, just leave them to Candace. Don't worry, she's as tough as they come.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After a while, the winds outside begin to calm.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The winds died down... That means the sandstorm's over, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Candace still isn't back yet, though. Is she alright? Maybe we should go out and check on her.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: When you put it that way, even I'm starting to feel a little worried... Alright, let's go. We've been here long enough, and the boys are as chatty as the floor.

choices.text: Is that enough to prove his innocence...?
Did you join forces with me just so you could investigate me?
The sages were watching me from the very beginning...
(What if that whole story was just made up?)

talks.objective: Check the situation outside the village chief's house

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Candace, you're still fighting? You've been out here dealing with these creatures the entire time?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Yes, they just keep coming in waves... I've lost count of how many I've defeated. Before I realized it, even the sandstorm had stopped...

choices.text: Not only is she really strong...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eek, here comes another wave!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Leave this round to us! I got interrupted earlier, but now I have something to take my anger out on!

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Hehe, it's been a while since I've seen the Flame-Mane in action. I'll leave these to you then.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: #I'll be sure to put on a good show! {NICKNAME}, let's go!

choices.text: Her stamina is also something else...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The creatures stopped appearing. Was that the last of them?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: What we fought just now was probably the aftermath of the sandstorm, so we should be safe for the time being.
Well fought, everyone. No injuries, I hope?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Who are you?
Ah, my apologies, I haven't had a chance to greet you yet. I had my hands full taking care of the village's elderly and children.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Anpu
dialogues.text: I am the chief of Aaru Village. Everyone usually calls me Uncle Anpu.

choices.text: It's a pleasure to meet you.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Sir, I am also originally from the desert, but I have not been back for some time now. May I ask if such sandstorms are common?

response.speaker: Uncle Anpu
response.text: I can't say they've always been common, but recently, the storms have become increasingly severe and frequent.

response.speaker: Uncle Anpu
response.text: Besides sandstorms, we also occasionally get earthquakes... According to an investigator who stayed in the village a while ago, these unusual natural phenomena are related to the withering of Irminsul.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, another effect of Irminsul's withering...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... Irminsul's withering causes Withering Zones in the forest, and sandstorms and earthquakes here in the desert?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Everything in the natural world is inextricably connected to Irminsul. These "regional symptoms" can indeed be a reflection of Irminsul's present state.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: *sigh* Everyone in Aaru Village needs to take good care of themselves.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Uh, speaking of which, why haven't I seen a single Village Keeper since I got here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Village Keeper? Who are they? Village guards like Candace?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Does your curiosity know no bounds... "Village Keeper" is how Aaru Village refers to mad scholars exiled here by the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Most of them are scholars who lost their sanity after a period of training in the Avidya Forest.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: The Akademiya believes that their crazed mutterings may have a negative effect on the psyches of other scholars, so they're forcibly exiled to the desert... Though if you ask me, it's all a boatload of nonsense.

choices.text: Tighnari also brought this up before...

response.speaker: Uncle Anpu
response.text: Alas, that's exactly what we've been trying to investigate. One by one, the Village Keepers have been mysteriously disappearing without a trace...

response.speaker: Uncle Anpu
response.text: But no one in the village has ever seen them leave... If you're planning to stay around the village for the next few days, I'd appreciate it if you could keep an eye out for them.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...I've had encounters with those people in the past. I'll see what I can do to help.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: The matra are the ones responsible for their exile. Now that you're no longer with them, are you trying to alleviate your guilt and atone for your past sins? I'm fascinated by how you think.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Mock me if you will. But if you are guilty, I will eliminate you, regardless of my position or identity.

response.speaker: Uncle Anpu
response.text: Oh, you're the former General Mahamatra? You must be an expert in these kinds of investigations. Thank you for your help.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll help, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Is it because you're reminded of Haypasia, {NICKNAME}? These poor scholars, first they lose their sanity, now this... We need to help get them back home, safe and sound.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, uh... Is it really a good idea to tag along with Cyno? You seem like you really don't trust him.

choices.text: That's why this is a great opportunity to watch him.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I'll be grateful for the assistance. No doubt you will do a better job than some of my former subordinates.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Let's start by finding a spot to share what we know so far.

choices.text: It'll be fine. Dehya and the others are here, too.
Haypasia was also nearly exiled to the desert.
Sorry for all the trouble.

talks.objective: Exchange information with Cyno somewhere else

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Although I've sent myself into exile, I'm still doing essentially the same things as before...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Do you still have any questions for me before we start our investigation?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why do they refer to the mad scholars as Village Keepers?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: One of my former subordinates told me that this title has its origins in a strange incident.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The Akademiya has long exiled mad scholars to Aaru Village. A mysterious phenomenon exists here...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: When mad scholars first arrive, they are as incoherent and deranged as before. But after spending some time here, they invariably begin to calm down.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Initially, the people of Aaru Village greatly resented having to take in the mad scholars. But a strange incident one night changed that...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Aaru Village was struck by the strongest earthquake in living memory. Seeing buildings on the verge of collapse all around him, the then chief of the village was preparing to take everyone to safety...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Suddenly, he noticed a mad scholar crouching in a corner, caressing the ground with his hands. A soft, green light radiated from him, like a divine glow against the backdrop of night.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Despite the powerful tremors that ripped through the ground that night, all the houses remained upright, almost as if they had grown roots reaching deep into the ground. In the end, not a single building collapsed, and no one was hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: After that, the people of Aaru Village treated the mad scholars with greater kindness, and began to refer to them as the Village Keepers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #A soft, green light... A mad scholar protecting Aaru Village... Hmm, what do you make of it, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: It must have been Nahida's power.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks so, too! Actually, Cyno, do you know if any of the mad scholars continued to wear their Akasha Terminals at Aaru Village?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: In theory, they would continue wearing them so the Akademiya could still monitor their activities. With that said, the main Akasha system would no longer have any interaction with them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, no wonder! Everything makes sense, then! Add in the fact that they calmed down... It was probably Nahida who calmed them...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...If you are able to draw a conclusion from this one story alone, then it appears you possess much more information than I do.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: So, what do you make of the story?

choices.text: That mad scholar's power likely came from Lesser Lord Kusanali.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Really? Lesser Lord Kusanali...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What, you don't believe us? Lesser Lord Kusanali was definitely using the Akasha to give her power to the mad scholars...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: No, it's not so much that I don't believe you, I'm just struck by your reasoning...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Lesser Lord Kusanali, the current Dendro Archon... Is she really active in Sumeru?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: The Akademiya has always placed far greater importance on the late Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. They've more or less ignored Lesser Lord Kusanali, and I've never had any reason to doubt their views.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: In addition, I've never heard any stories about Lesser Lord Kusanali and her deeds... To me, she might as well have been a god that never existed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No way, Nahida definitely exists! She's a... How should Paimon put it... She's a good archon who's kind and wise! ...Even if she says weird stuff sometimes!

choices.text: She also saved me once not long ago.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I've spent many years interrogating criminals, so I can easily tell when someone is lying.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good! Then you should know that we're telling the truth!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: That look in your eyes... I've never seen that from a liar. You two really must have met Lesser Lord Kusanali.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...How can this be...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: To think, our archon has been among us this entire time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, now it's our turn to put our skills to good use for this investigation!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You betcha!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But easier said than done, especially since we don't have any leads... Hmm... Maybe we can start by knocking on some doors?
Excuse me, are you here to help me find my grandpa?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Who are you?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: By the sounds of it... a resident of this village.

response.speaker: Isak
response.text: M—My name is Isak... You'll help me find my grandpa, right?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Is your grandpa a mad scholar?

response.speaker: Isak
response.text: Hey, don't say that! Grandpa is just Grandpa. Why do you have to call him that... It's not like he's a bad person or anything.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: The person you're referring to is not a local, yet you are. Why do you call him "Grandpa"?

response.speaker: Isak
response.text: Grandpa is just Grandpa! He's my family.

response.speaker: Isak
response.text: I heard everything you said to the village chief. Please, you gotta take me with you! I wanna find my grandpa, I swear I'll help... I won't be a nuisance!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Ah, so you're the one who was eavesdropping on us around the village chief's house.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I was planning to go out and take care of whoever it was, but I had a vague feeling that they didn't harbor any ill intent...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, Alhaitham wasn't kidding about matra having sharp senses... Cyno, he's just a kid! All he wants is to find his grandpa. Let's find a way to help him!

response.speaker: Isak
response.text: Sorry... I was only listening in because I wanted to know where Grandpa went, honest! If you don't believe me, you can ask Miss Candace.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Please help him, Cyno.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...Alright. But first, let's confirm the facts with Candace.

choices.text: We saved Sumeru City together in the not-so distant past.
Lesser Lord Kusanali was actually the one who protected the village.
Only she could be capable of that...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you approach the village chief's house, Cyno asks Isak to wait nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cyno is super vigilant... Is this what all the matra are like?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Ah, you're back already.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We just wanted to confirm something with you. Do you know a boy by the name of Isak?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Hehe, I had a feeling he'd go looking for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You knew this would happen?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Yes. Although he tried his best to stay hidden, I still noticed him eavesdropping outside the window. He really wants to get his grandfather back.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Isak's parents were both Eremite mercenaries who rarely returned to the village after finding employment in the city. He was raised by his grandfather.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, it was only a few years before his grandpa passed away. Isak was still very young at the time, so various families in the village took turns caring for him so he could survive.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Later, an elderly mad scholar arrived in the village. Isak thought the scholar bore a striking resemblance to his grandfather, and thus often spied on the man.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: However, the scholar was unkempt in appearance and incoherent in speech. Although Isak referred to the man as his "grandpa," he was afraid and didn't dare to approach him.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: One summer night, the oft-mumbling and bumbling "grandpa" suddenly calmed down and seemed to become more lucid. He even noticed Isak hiding in the distance.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: So "Grandpa" walked up to Isak and patted him on the head. He even took Isak to the entrance of the village, where he patiently taught the boy the names of the stars, and accompanied Isak until he fell asleep.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: The next morning, Isak woke up and wanted to go find his "grandpa" again, only to realize his grandpa no longer recognized him. However, even so, Grandpa retained his calm expression.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: It's said that those who saw the scholar claimed he no longer appeared to be crazy, but appeared to be living in his own world, almost as if he were sleepwalking.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Isak was thrilled that his "grandpa" was able to find peace, and would follow him all the time asking him things like, "Grandpa, want me to take you somewhere fun?" or "Grandpa, could you tell me stories about the stars again?"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All this somehow just makes Paimon feel really sad... It seems like they both deserve so much better...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Perhaps. Nearly everyone who lives in the desert has some form of hardship or regret. But even so, we must still continue on with our lives.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: It's also my reason for fighting. I must continue to protect this land.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ("Lucid grandpa" was probably Nahida... She must have soothed the other mad scholars as well.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (From the look on Cyno's face, he's probably connected the dots as well.)

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Maybe the people have always had a considerate god watching over them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What did you say, Cyno?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No, nothing. As long as Isak keeps his word and doesn't get in our way, we can take him along.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Perhaps you are more compassionate than I gave you credit for. Please accept my thanks on Isak's behalf, Cyno.

talks.objective: Go to the village chief's house

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Isak!

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you guys!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've cleared everything up! Let's go find your grandpa!

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Really!? Wow, thank you so much!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your grandpa will be found safe and sound.

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Yeah!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Alright, let's ask the local residents some questions first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alhaitham went that way — let's hurry up and follow him. Wonder what he's up to...
